description: Wisconsin-only statute items, plus 20 Class D practice items taken from a Wisconsin DOT practice-test result and cited to the Motorists' Handbook page. National driving rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Handbook diagrams are not copied.

questions.q: Wisconsin's 70 mph freeway limit, including interstate freeways, is in force when
options: Official signs giving notice of that limit have been erected
The road is rural, even if no speed sign is posted
Every expressway automatically uses 70 with or without signs
A city has not adopted a 55 mph ordinance
questions.explanation: Section 346.57(4)(gm)2 sets 70 mph on freeways, including interstate freeways, and on an expressway that uses only interchanges. Section 346.57(6)(b) says that limit is not effective until official signs are posted.
questions.remember: Freeway 70 applies once the signs are up.

questions.q: When you pass a Wisconsin schoolhouse while children are going to or from school, or playing in the sidewalk area at the school, the limit is
options: 25 mph unless a school-zone beacon is dark
10 mph only while a bus is stopped
questions.explanation: Section 346.57(4)(a) sets 15 mph when passing a schoolhouse at those times. A marked school crossing has its own 15 mph rule under (4)(b) when a child is present, a guard is in the crossing, or a guard is placing or removing a traffic device.
questions.remember: Passing a school with kids around: 15.

questions.q: If no other fixed Wisconsin speed limit applies and no limit is posted, the limit is
questions.explanation: Section 346.57(4)(h) sets 55 mph in the absence of any other fixed limit or the posting of a limit. A signed freeway, expressway, school, alley, or city limit replaces that default.

questions.q: The statutory limit on a Wisconsin expressway, other than a portion that uses interchanges only, is
options: 70 mph even when no sign is posted
25 mph inside any city the expressway crosses
65 mph where official signs give notice of that limit
questions.explanation: Section 346.57(4)(gm)1 sets 65 mph on an expressway. Subdivision 2 raises a through-traffic, interchange-only portion to 70. Subsection (6)(b) requires signs before either expressway figure is effective.

questions.q: On a Wisconsin city or village street that is not an outlying district and is not a state or county trunk, the limit unless a sign shows another number is
questions.explanation: Section 346.57(4)(e) sets 25 mph inside a city or village, other than an outlying district. Outlying districts are 35 under (4)(f). On state trunk, connecting, and county trunk highways, (6)(a) also requires official signs before the 25 or 35 limit is effective.

questions.q: The speed limit in a Wisconsin alley is
questions.explanation: Section 346.57(4)(d) sets 15 mph in any alley. That is the same number as the schoolhouse limit, but it is a separate rule.

questions.q: For a Wisconsin driver with two or fewer prior OWI-related convictions, suspensions, or revocations, the prohibited alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: Section 340.01(46m)(a) sets 0.08 or more when the driver has two or fewer priors counted under s. 343.307(1). Three or more priors, or an ignition-interlock order under s. 343.301, drops that figure to more than 0.02.

questions.q: Wisconsin's absolute-sobriety rule treats a driver under 21 as in violation when the alcohol concentration is
options: 0.08 or more and not before that
0.02 or more and not a lower result
More than 0.0 but not more than 0.08
questions.explanation: Section 346.63(2m) applies when a driver who has not reached the legal drinking age has an alcohol concentration of more than 0.0 but not more than 0.08. A result of 0.08 or more is the general prohibited-alcohol offense under s. 340.01(46m). Wisconsin does not use another state's 0.02 underage figure for this rule.
questions.remember: Under 21: any alcohol is a violation.

questions.q: Wisconsin sets a prohibited alcohol concentration of more than 0.02 for a driver who
options: Has 3 or more countable prior convictions, suspensions, or revocations, or is under an ignition-interlock order
Is any driver age 21 or older
Is under 21, instead of the more-than-0.0 rule
Is driving a passenger car for the first time
questions.explanation: Section 340.01(46m)(c) uses more than 0.02, not 0.02 exactly and not the first-offense 0.08 figure. It covers both the repeat-offender count and a driver subject to an order under s. 343.301.

questions.q: Wisconsin suspends an ordinary operating privilege when demerit points for violations committed within any 12-month period reach
questions.explanation: Trans 101.04(1) requires suspension at 12 points for violations committed within any 12-month period. The department uses the violation date, not a later court date.

questions.q: An ordinary Wisconsin license, not a probationary license or instruction permit, is suspended for 2 months when the 12-month demerit total is
questions.explanation: Trans 101.04(3) sets 2 months for 12 to 16 points, 4 months for 17 to 22, 6 months for 23 to 30, and 1 year for more than 30. Permit and probationary drivers use the different table in (3m).

questions.q: A driver who holds a Wisconsin instruction permit or probationary license and gathers 12 to 30 demerit points in 12 months is suspended for
options: 2 months, the same as an ordinary license at 12 points
questions.explanation: Trans 101.04(3m) sets 6 months for 12 to 30 points and 1 year for more than 30. Trans 101.02(7) doubles a later conviction only if that person already has a prior demerit conviction. Chapter 347 equipment violations are not doubled. A first conviction is not automatically doubled.
questions.remember: Permit or probationary, 12 to 30 points: 6 months.

questions.q: A Wisconsin instruction-permit holder may drive only with a front-seat accompanier who has two years of licensed experience, a valid regular license, and who is
options: Any licensed driver, including a probationary driver sitting in the back seat
A person who holds a permit of their own
A qualified instructor age 19 or older; a parent, guardian, or spouse age 19 or older; or a person age 21 or older, with written permission if the permit holder is under 18
questions.explanation: Section 343.07 requires that person to sit beside the permit holder. During hours of darkness the accompanier must be a qualified instructor or a licensed driver age 25 or older with at least two years of experience.
questions.remember: Permit driving: a qualified adult beside you.

questions.q: Wisconsin issues a probationary Class D license to a driver under 18 only if that driver is at least 16 and has
options: Held an instruction permit at least 6 months and had no moving-violation conviction in those 6 months
Finished one day of classroom instruction and no permit
Already held a regular license in Wisconsin
Reached 18, because probationary licenses start then
questions.explanation: Section 343.085(1) issues a probationary license to original applicants, with exemptions such as a commercial license. Under 18, subsection (1)(b) also requires age 16, six months on an instruction permit, and no disqualifying moving conviction in that period.
questions.remember: Probationary license: permit 6 months, no moving violations.

questions.q: During the first 9 months of a Wisconsin probationary license, a driver under 18 may drive between midnight and 5 a.m. only if
options: A parent or guardian, or another qualified accompanying driver, sits beside them, or the trip is between home, school, and work
The restriction ends at 9 p.m. instead
Another driver under 18 rides along as the supervisor
The trip is on a freeway, where the restriction does not apply
questions.explanation: Section 343.085(2m)(a)2 is midnight to 5 a.m. Emergency driving is excluded. The same nine months also limit extra passengers under (2m)(a)1. The restriction ends when the period ends or the driver turns 18, whichever comes first.
questions.remember: Midnight to 5 a.m.: only with a qualified adult.

questions.q: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light:
options: Slow down and proceed with caution
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. The handbook practice quiz answer is C.
questions.remember: Flashing yellow: slow, go with care.

questions.q: When turning left at an intersection:
options: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.
questions.remember: Turning left? Oncoming and walkers go first.

questions.q: If you find yourself in a skid:
questions.explanation: Stay off the brakes in a skid. Look and steer where you want the car to go. A hard or sudden brake can make the skid worse.
questions.remember: Skid: off the brake, steer where you want to go.

questions.q: If you are parked downhill, which way do you turn the front wheels?
options: All the way to the left
All the way to the right
questions.explanation: Downhill, turn the front wheels all the way to the right, toward the curb or roadside. Then set the parking brake. Uphill with a curb, turn them left.

questions.q: In general when driving, how often should you check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you?
questions.explanation: Check the rearview mirror about every 6 to 8 seconds so you know what is behind you before you brake or change lanes.
questions.why: Checking the mirror shows you whether someone is following too closely.

questions.q: Which of the following road surfaces freeze first and tend to thaw last?
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze first and thaw last because cold air reaches them from above and below. Slow down on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.q: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: Oncoming cars moving straight ahead or turning right
questions.explanation: A left turn yields to oncoming cars going straight or turning right. Handbook practice quiz answer C.

questions.q: If you are stopped and the officer suspects you have been drinking, you can refuse the BAC test:
options: If you think you will fail.
questions.explanation: Wisconsin's implied-consent rule means a driver arrested on suspicion of impaired driving does not get to refuse the chemical test. Refusal has its own penalties.
questions.remember: Arrested? You can't refuse the test.

questions.q: If you are wanting to pass a bicycle, but there is an oncoming vehicle approaching, you should:
options: Slow down and let the car pass, then pass the bicycle
Pull over to the side of the road and stop
Speed up to pass the bicycle before the car approaches
questions.explanation: Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicycle. Do not squeeze the rider or rush the pass.
questions.remember: Car coming? Let it pass, then pass the bike.

questions.q: Backing can be dangerous. What speed is recommended for backing?
options: No faster than a slow crawl.
No faster than a slow walk.
No faster than a slow jog.
No faster than a slow run.
questions.explanation: Back no faster than a slow walk. That speed leaves time to stop if a person or a car enters the path behind you.

questions.q: You are merging onto an interstate highway. You should:
options: Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.
Merge over two lanes at once and speed up.
Always stop before entering the highway
questions.explanation: Use the ramp to match highway speed, signal, and merge into a gap. Do not stop on the ramp when traffic is moving, and do not cross two lanes at once.
questions.remember: Merging: find a gap and slide in.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages with no posted speed limit?
questions.explanation: Where no limit is posted, the maximum speed in the outlying parts of a city or village is 35 mph.

questions.q: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: Oncoming cars moving straight ahead or turning right
questions.explanation: A left turn yields to oncoming cars going straight or turning right. Handbook practice quiz answer C.

questions.q: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?
options: You may pass if safe to do so
The lanes are going in opposite directions
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates opposite directions and allows a pass when it is safe. The handbook answer is both.
questions.remember: Dashed yellow: opposite directions, passing allowed.

questions.q: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop:
options: Only until the children are out of the bus
Until the lights stop flashing and there are no children around
If the bus is on the same side of the road as you are
questions.explanation: Stop until the red lights stop flashing and no children are around. On an undivided road this applies to both directions.
questions.remember: Red lights flashing: stay stopped till kids are clear.

questions.q: When is it OK to drive faster than the posted speed limit?
options: If you do not see any other traffic in your lane
questions.explanation: A posted limit is the maximum. You may need to drive slower, but not faster.
questions.remember: The posted limit is a maximum.

questions.q: How far down the road should you look when driving?
options: Only as far as the vehicle ahead
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead. If you cannot see that far, slow down.
questions.why: If you can't see that far ahead, slowing down gives you better control.

questions.q: Use the four-second following distance rule by:
options: Counting four seconds after the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object before you reach it
Staying four car lengths behind at any speed
Matching the speed of the vehicle ahead
Dropping back only in a school zone
questions.explanation: Pick a stationary object. When the vehicle ahead passes it, you should not reach that object for at least four seconds.
questions.remember: Count four seconds past a fixed point.

questions.q: You are following a motorcycle. You should:
options: Follow at the same gap you would use for a car
Move up close so other drivers can see both of you
Leave extra room, because a motorcycle can stop faster than most vehicles
Pass in the same lane, beside the motorcycle
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are light and can stop faster than most vehicles. Leave extra room when you follow one, check blind spots, and wait until it is safe to pass.
questions.why: Motorcycles are light and can stop faster than most vehicles.

questions.q: If your tires start to hydroplane, you should:
options: Ease off the gas, hold the wheel straight, and do not brake or turn until the tires grip again
Brake hard and steer toward the shoulder
Accelerate so the tires cut through the water
Shift to neutral and pump the brakes
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning means the tires are riding on the water. Ease off the gas, keep the wheel straight, and wait until the tires grip before you brake or turn.
questions.remember: Hydroplaning: off the gas, wheel straight.

questions.q: In Wisconsin, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: In Wisconsin, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Wisconsin, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: In Wisconsin, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 19 years.

provenance.manual: WisDOT Instruction permit, probationary license and regular license

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Wisconsin car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Wisconsin car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: WisDOT New online knowledge test news release

questions.q: In Wisconsin, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

questions.q: In Wisconsin, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Wisconsin brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Wisconsin, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Wisconsin?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Wisconsin can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Wisconsin rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: How is Wisconsin's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
questions.explanation: Wisconsin seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Wisconsin?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Wisconsin: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is Wisconsin's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $10,000.

questions.q: Under Wisconsin's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Wisconsin can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 12 months.
